[[Image:University of Denver skiing at the WH.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The [[Denver Pioneers ski team|Denver Pioneers]]<!-- men's and women's teams--> at the [[White House]] with [[President of the United States|President]] [[George W. Bush]] in June [[2008 in sports|2008]]. Through 2020, Denver owns the most team titles at 24.<!-- 24 thru 2020 -->]]
The '''NCAA Skiing Championships''' are held annually to crown the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] combined men's and women's team [[skiing]] champion. Before 1983, the championship was only for men's skiing. Unlike many NCAA sports, only one [[National Collegiate]] championship is held each season with teams from [[NCAA Division I|Division I]], [[NCAA Division II|Division II]], and [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] competing together.<ref>{{cite web |title=NATIONAL COLLEGIATE SKIING CHAMPIONSHIPS RECORDS BOOK |url=http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/skiing_champs_records/NC.pdf |website=ncaa.org |publisher=NCAA |access-date=11 January 2025}}</ref>

The [[Denver Pioneers ski team|University of Denver]] has won a record 24 team titles, including ten<!-- championships--> since 2000. The [[Colorado Buffaloes ski team|University of Colorado]] is second<!-- all time--> with 20 titles (plus one [[Association for Intercollegiate Athletics for Women|AIAW]] title), and the [[Utah Utes ski team|University of Utah]] is third with 16 <!-- national championships--> (plus one AIAW title).<!-- 12 thru 2020 -->

Denver won the first<!-- ever--> NCAA championship in [[1954 NCAA Skiing Championships|1954]] at [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]] with 384 points,<ref name=dcslc>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=vIlaAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9UkDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5242%2C1234904 |work=Deseret News |location=Salt Lake City, Utah |agency=United Press |last=Bennyhoff |first=Robert |title=Denver cops national ski tourney |date=March 8, 1954 |page=B4}}</ref> 34.4 points ahead of runner-up [[Seattle Redhawks|Seattle University]]<!-- at 349.6-->.<ref name=trskmx>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=WHgpAAAAIBAJ&sjid=N-YDAAAAIBAJ&pg=2530%2C253424 |work=Spokesman-Review |location=Spokane, Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=Cougars, Vandals trail in ski mix |date=March 7, 1954 |page=2, sports}}</ref><ref name=dskbrd>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=WXgpAAAAIBAJ&sjid=N-YDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3194%2C1013435 |work=Spokesman-Review |location=Spokane, Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=Denver ski birds win NCAA jump; Vandals fourth |date=March 8, 1954 |page=8}}</ref> The scoring system has been modified over the years; in <!--[[2012 NCAA Skiing Championships|2012]]-->2012, [[Vermont Catamounts ski team|Vermont]] scored a record 832 points,<!-- the most ever by an NCAA champion,--> with a record margin of 161 points over second-place [[Utah Utes ski team|Utah]].<!--, which finished with 671 points-->

The 2020 edition started on schedule, but was canceled in progress due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cubuffs.com/documents/2020/3/27/2020_NCAA_Championship_Results_FINAL.pdf|title=2020 NCAA Championship Results FINAL (PDF)|website=University of Colorado Athletics}}</ref>

==Appearances by team==

'''Key'''
* {{color box|#FFA500|'''CH'''|border=#AA5000}} National Champion
* {{color box|#ACACAC|RU}} National Runner-up
* Numbers indicate the placement of the team in that tournament beyond second
* The 2020 championships were abandoned due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], so team appearances are credited, but no placements.
